title: Minimum Sum of Mountain Triplets I
summary: Given an array nums, find the minimum sum of indices (i, j, k) where i < j < k, and nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k].
statement: Given an array nums, find the minimum sum of indices (i, j, k) where i < j < k, and nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k]. If no such triplet exists, return -1.
constraints: Choose indices i<j<k such that nums[i] and nums[k] are both strictly smaller than nums[j].
Return -1 when no mountain triplet exists.
hints: For each possible middle index, only the smallest value on each side can minimize its triplet.
Build the exclusive prefix minimum for every position.
Scan from right to left while maintaining the exclusive suffix minimum, testing both strict inequalities.
Any valid triplet using a middle j is no better than the two side minima, so minimizing these candidates is globally optimal.
